stem: Stretching a rubber band, compressing a spring, and moulding clay into a new shape are all examples of a force causing a change in an object's:
explanation: Force can change an object's shape (deformation) in addition to changing its state of motion (speed or direction) — stretching, compressing, and moulding are all shape-changing effects of applied force.

section: Science (Paper-2) · Ch — Force, Pressure & Motion — Deep 2
subject: Science
stem: A person walking on soft, wet mud sinks in more than a person of the same weight standing on a wooden plank laid over the same mud. This is best explained by the fact that the plank:

options.option_text: Increases the surface area of contact, thereby reducing the pressure exerted on the mud for the same total force (weight)
Increases the force exerted by the person
Has no effect on pressure or sinking at all

explanation: Since Pressure = Force / Area, spreading the same weight (force) over a larger area (the plank) reduces the pressure exerted at any single point, so the person sinks less — the same principle behind snow-shoes and wide tyres on soft ground.
